name: A Day to Remember
label: Victory
lede: A Day to Remember played seven shows in its first year in Ocala, Florida, then signed to Victory Records, covered Kelly Clarkson, sued the label, released its own album mid-lawsuit and won a verdict.

eras.title: Seven shows in Ocala
eras.text: A Day to Remember came out of Ocala, Florida, mashing pop-punk choruses into metalcore breakdowns. The first year was barely a band; by 2005 it had a label and a debut album.

years.h: Five kids in Ocala start a band and play seven shows in year one
years.p: Jeremy McKinnon sings, Neil Westfall and Tom Denney play guitar, Joshua Woodard plays bass and Bobby Scruggs drums.

years.h: Halos for Heros, Dirt for the Dead is the first thing they put out
years.p: A self-released EP, followed in January 2005 by a six-song demo.

years.h: Indianola signs the band in February; And Their Name Was Treason follows in May
years.p: The debut sells over 10,000 copies.

eras.title: Victory comes calling, Ron Jeremy shows up
eras.text: A friend of Joshua Woodard's had a line to Victory Records, and that got the band onto the Chicago label. The debut came with a porn-star cameo, and its reissue carried a Kelly Clarkson cover that became a calling card.

years.big: "We IM'ed back and forth for about six months."
years.h: Instant messages land the band a deal with Victory
years.p: Woodard's friend had the AIM screenname of someone at the label. The signing was announced August 11, and Alex Shelnutt replaces Scruggs on drums this year.
years.xp: Woodard recalled that a friend said he had the AIM screenname of someone at Victory Records, and that the two then IM'ed back and forth for about six months before the band got to the label.

years.h: For Those Who Have Heart is the Victory debut
years.p: Recorded at Zing Studios in Westfield, Massachusetts, with Eric Arena. It reaches No. 17 on Billboard's Heatseekers and sells 20,000 by September.
play: The Plot to Bomb the Panhandle

years.h: Ron Jeremy turns up in the video for The Plot to Bomb the Panhandle
years.p: The adult-film star's cameo is in the band's first Victory video.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Day to Remember · Wikipedia: For Those Who Have Heart
years.h: Victory reissues For Those Who Have Heart with a Kelly Clarkson cover
years.p: Since U Been Gone arrives with a DVD of a January 5, 2008 show at The Capitol in Ocala. The reissue charts at No. 43 on Independent Albums, and the video follows in July.
years.xp: The band had posted its version of Since U Been Gone on MySpace in September 2007, months before the reissue.

years.h: Homesick gets written on Warped Tour and the Easycore Tour
years.p: Chad Gilbert of [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] produces the recording. Kerrang! nominates the band for Best International Newcomer; Black Tide wins.

eras.title: Homesick and a Top 20
eras.text: Homesick sold 200,000 copies by July 2010 and What Separates Me from You reached No. 11. One founding guitarist left to focus on his family, and Kevin Skaff of Four Letter Lie stayed for good.

years.src: Wikipedia: Homesick (A Day to Remember album)
yt: The Downfall of Us All video
I'm Made of Wax, Larry, What Are You Made Of? video
years.h: Homesick lands at No. 21 and tops the indie chart
years.p: Recorded at The Wade Studio in Ocala with Gilbert. It sells 22,000 in its first week and 200,000 by July 2010, and goes gold in 2016.
years.xp:
Guests include Mike Hranica of [[The Devil Wears Prada|43c0958c-27ef-46c4-b4cc-83cfca54170d]], Vincent Bennett of [[The Acacia Strain|08bebce9-33fa-4ae9-9992-4e5d137d655b]] and Sierra Kusterbeck of VersaEmerge. McKinnon said the closer If It Means a Lot to You took nearly a year to finish.

Have Faith in Me reached No. 40 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart in 2010.

years.h: Denney leaves; Kevin Skaff of Four Letter Lie takes over
years.p: Denney wanted to focus on his marriage, family and recording studio, and stayed involved in writing. Skaff becomes the permanent guitarist.

yt: Mr. Highway's Thinking About The End video
years.h: What Separates Me from You hits No. 11
years.p: Partly recorded, per the credits, on the back of a bus with no AC in Germany and in a closet in New Jersey. It sells 80,000 by December and goes gold in 2016.

eras.title: The band sues, then releases it anyway
eras.text: The band said Victory owed it royalties; Victory said the band wanted out of a five-album deal for a major. While the case dragged on, A Day to Remember built a studio in Jeremy McKinnon's house and put out its own record.

years.cap: A Day to Remember live, July 24, 2011
years.h: Jimmy Kimmel Live! gives the band its national TV debut
years.p: They play All I Want and Better Off This Way, then head out on the Game Changers Tour with [[Bring Me the Horizon|074e3847-f67f-49f9-81f1-8c8cea147e8e]] in March.

years.big: "...no intention of speaking publicly or disparagingly regarding their disagreement with Victory."
years.src: Wikipedia: A Day to Remember · Wikipedia: Common Courtesy · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: A Day to Remember says Victory owes it over $75,000
years.p: The band's statement, issued as it announced the suit it had filed May 31, 2011. Victory said the real issue was the band refusing to deliver five albums and wanting a major label.
years.xp:
The band said Victory owed it over $75,000 in royalties. Victory's answer was that the band wanted out of a five-album deal for a major.

Victory had been through a public split before: [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]] left for Island in 2002 after its own fight with founder Tony Brummel.

years.h: Violence (Enough Is Enough) leaks unmixed
years.p: McKinnon said he wanted it dark and ominous, about things being out of your hands; some fans heard it as a lawsuit song.

yt: Right Back At It Again video
years.h: A court clears the way, and Common Courtesy comes out four days later
years.p: On October 4 a court let the band release its own album while the case continued. It went out digitally October 8 on ADTR Records; physical copies followed November 25.
years.xp:
It was made in a studio built in McKinnon's Orlando home, later called Wade Studios, from early 2012 to March 2013. McKinnon and producer Andrew Wade put in $40,000 and the rest of the band $20,000. Gilbert co-produced.

It sold 92,874 copies in its first week (40,550 digital, 52,324 physical), reached No. 37 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on the UK Rock & Metal chart, and had sold 270,000 in the US by July 2016. Metacritic gave it 80.

The ruling still left the band owing Victory at least two more albums.

eras.title: A festival, an award and a verdict
eras.text: McKinnon started his own festival, the band won Best Live Band, and in 2016 the Victory case ended with a verdict. Ocala handed the band the keys to the city.

years.h: McKinnon's own festival opens at the NOS Event Center
years.p: The first Self Help Fest, in San Bernardino, has [[Bring Me the Horizon|074e3847-f67f-49f9-81f1-8c8cea147e8e]], [[Of Mice & Men|82b6784e-8161-42a0-9b5c-b9d31e63fd85]] and [[The Story So Far|bc303c9e-3ffb-49ca-acf1-088ef4d46ed7]]. It runs through 2017.

years.cap: A Day to Remember live at Rock am Ring, Germany
years.h: The band headlines the Parks & Devastation Tour
years.p: Bring Me the Horizon, [[Motionless in White|1c5b9bd6-76e8-4fe7-a6df-3bc0b5a452cc]] and [[Chiodos|b755836a-0cb6-4577-a678-55a5a6402d70]] share the bill.

years.h: Best Live Band at the Alternative Press Music Awards
years.p: A year after three nominations, including Artist of the Year, the band takes the live award.

years.cap: A Day to Remember live at Saratoga Performing Arts Center, New York, September 4, 2016
years.h: Bad Vibrations lands on Epitaph in the middle of a Blink-182 tour
years.p: The first album on Epitaph Records comes out while the band supports [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] on its July to October 2016 tour.

years.h: The band beats Victory in court, taking three of four issues
years.p: Wikipedia's Victory Records article says the band was awarded $4.02 million.

years.h: Ocala hands the band the keys to the city
years.p: Presented at the March 18 homecoming show in Ocala.

eras.title: A bassist leaves, an album appears
eras.text: A Day to Remember moved to Fueled by Ramen and worked with Marshmello. Its founding bassist left in 2021, and in 2025 the band dropped an album with no warning.

years.h: Rescue Me pairs the band with [[Marshmello|301b45a4-b8b9-410e-8344-4b4eaf96691a]]
years.p: The collaboration with the EDM producer is the band's first new release in three years.

years.h: You're Welcome comes out on Fueled by Ramen
years.p: The band's seventh studio album.

years.h: Joshua Woodard, a founding member, leaves the band
years.p: Per Wikipedia, he left over allegations of past sexual misconduct. It also emerged that in 2017 Woodard crossed three lanes of traffic in a crash that killed a 24-year-old driver.

years.h: Big Ole Album Vol. 1 arrives with no warning
years.p: A surprise self-release with singles Make It Make Sense and LeBron. It came out on physical formats first; streaming followed March 21.
